mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average signals weakening aggregate demand with partial offset from housing activity, resulting in muted S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > 12-month MA
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during episodes matching the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending power and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained INDPRO contraction as defined.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in CPIAUCSL below 2% while FEDFUNDS remains below 1% signals a deflationary bias with accommodative policy, which increases risk appetite and boosts S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% AND FEDFUNDS < 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive during episodes meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average combined with a rising RSAFS (retail sales) above its 6-month moving average signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA AND RSAFS > 6-month MA for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods matching the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly rise in the unemployment rate below 4% for six consecutive months signals an unusually tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained low unemployment as defined.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals an expansion in manufacturing output, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained INDPRO expansion as defined.
